hazard: Inadequate medical review of drivers with deteriorating health
areas: Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
Kingston Upon Hull and the East Riding of Yorkshire

reports.title: Henry Prow
reports.area: Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly

concerns.quote: criteria required by the DVLA and Department of Transport for the issuing and surrendering of driving licences and the terms and conditions for ensuring appropriate modification of driver's vehicles
concerns.hazard: inadequate medical review of drivers with deteriorating health

concerns.quote: no mechanism for ensuring the required modification to the vehicles were still relevant to the vehicle that they were driving at the time
concerns.hazard: vehicle modifications not updated to match current vehicle and health status

concerns.quote: driver's GP/doctors could have a conflict of interests in such situations as they would have a duty to inform the DVLA of medical issues which could result in the surrender of the driving licence
concerns.hazard: conflict of interest between medical duty and licence surrender

reports.title: Billy Warwick-Jones: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

promises.quote: we have contacted the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) to alert them to these issues, so they can consider how best to raise awareness of this particular case and its implications with their members.
promises.summary: Contact RCGP to raise awareness of UTI-related delirium risks in older drivers

concerns.quote: The driver of the vehicle that caused this death was unwell with a urine tract infection. He had previously been treated for a urine tract infection. There is no evidence to suggest that he or his family were advised that he may demonstrate symptoms of confusion, agitation or delirium as a consequence of this and they would render him unfit to drive.
concerns.hazard: unwell driver with untreated urinary tract infection causing delirium

concerns.quote: There appears to be insufficient testing and instruction of the older population with regards to road safety, which led to this tragic outcome. While there are guidelines for driving with dementia or mild cognitive impairment produced by the General Medical Council, there appears to be nothing specific to other sudden onset confusion or delirium which is a well recognised and common symptom in the elderly when physically unwell.
concerns.hazard: lack of testing and instruction for older drivers regarding sudden confusion or delirium

concerns.quote: Consideration should be given to more frequent, rigorous testing and to consider the duties that should be placed on the driver, their medical practitioners and also family members/carers to report changes in presentation or health to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency.
concerns.hazard: need for more frequent testing and reporting duties

reports.title: Geoffrey Toase and Michael Midgley: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
reports.area: Kingston Upon Hull and the East Riding of Yorkshire

promises.quote: the DVLA can also issue a licence for a shorter period, typically between one and five years, allowing driving fitness to be more regularly monitored
promises.summary: Issue shorter licences for regular fitness checks

concerns.quote: DVLA Doctors are not actively encouraged by the DVLA to request further information about an applicant's medical history
concerns.hazard: lack of encouragement to request medical history

concerns.quote: The DVLA does not generally seek further information from any identified Speciality Doctor that may be involved in an applicant's medical care and treatment; any requests for further information are usually directed to an applicant's General Practitioner (GP)
concerns.hazard: failure to seek specialist medical information

concerns.quote: The forms sent to an applicant's GP by the DVLA for the purpose of obtaining further information are largely tick box in nature and do not provide sufficient scope for the GP to provide more detailed information and this therefore does not allow for a full assessment to be conducted by the reviewing DVLA Doctor
Current DVLA working practices do not appear to allow DVLA Doctors to consider the interplay between different medical conditions an applicant may be suffering with
concerns.hazard: inability to assess combined medical conditions

concerns.quote: There is no apparent system in place to verify the accuracy of the information provided by an applicant within their medical self-declaration and that this information is generally accepted by the DVLA without question

The information provided by an applicant within their medical self-declaration is no longer sent to their GP by the DVLA alongside any request for further information, which limits any scope for the GP to identify if the information contained within a medical self-declaration is accurate

reports.title: Christopher Sampson: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: I heard evidence in this inquest concerning the requirement of drivers' to self-notify the DVLA of any medical conditions that may interfere with their driving
concerns.hazard: drivers failing to self-report medical conditions to DVLA

concerns.quote: Furthermore, the driver's medical records were ambiguous as to whether he had been explicitly told to notify the DVLA of his health conditions
concerns.hazard: ambiguous medical records regarding DVLA notification

concerns.quote: The issue of drivers failing to self-refer their health issues to the DVLA for assessment is a serious and persisting issue
concerns.hazard: drivers not self-referring health issues to DVLA

concerns.quote: Drivers may not self-report medical conditions due to a variety of reasons
concerns.hazard: lack of awareness or understanding of DVLA notification duties

links.explanation: Both reports highlight shortcomings in the DVLA's medical assessment processes for drivers, specifically the lack of thorough review of applicants' health conditions.
links.earlier_quote: The DVLA appears to have limited mechanisms for drivers to be formally medically reviewed for the purpose of being medically fit to drive.
links.later_quote: Current DVLA working practices do not appear to allow DVLA Doctors to consider the interplay between different medical conditions an applicant may be suffering with.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight insufficient mechanisms for ensuring drivers remain medically fit to drive and for reporting health changes to the DVLA.

links.later_quote: Consideration should be given to more frequent, rigorous testing and to consider the duties that should be placed on the driver, their medical practitioners and also family members/carers to report changes in presentation or health to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the problem that drivers' medical conditions are not being reported to the DVLA, which can lead to unsafe driving. They share the concern that current mechanisms for reporting health changes are insufficient.
links.earlier_quote: Consideration should be given to more frequent, rigorous testing and to consider the duties that should be placed on the driver, their medical practitioners and also family members/carers to report changes in presentation or health to the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency.
links.later_quote: Drivers may not self-report medical conditions due to a variety of reasons. This can be due to due to a lack of understanding, insight, or simply because someone has not explicitly told them what to do or how to do it
